If your horse fights the bridle, pops his head at the gate, or just feels like he's arguing with you through every turn — before you blame the bit or the training, check the poll. A locked atlas sits right at the base of the skull. It limits rotation, creates discomfort under contact, and makes a willing horse look like a problem horse. Dr. Leo finds poll restriction in the majority of first-time exams on performance horses across DFW and North Texas. It's not attitude. It's anatomy. We come to your barn — no trailering required.
